clinician.trajectory_summary: An 86-year-old male with hypertension, kidney stones, and hypothyroidism presented to the ED with acute worsening of chronic lower back and right lower extremity pain and numbness that had been progressive over 9-10 months and was initially attributed to sciatica but unresponsive to treatment. On admission, urinalysis revealed pyuria and microscopic hematuria (E002). Laboratory studies showed leukocytosis (WBC 20.57), anemia (Hgb 10.5), acute kidney injury (BUN 44, Cr 1.7 from baseline 1.1), and elevated lactate 3.7 (E001). MRI of the lumbar spine demonstrated acute insufficiency fractures involving S1, S2, and left sacral ala, a T1 low and T2 bright signal mass in the L3 vertebral body suspicious for metastatic lesion, moderate-to-severe left hydroureteronephrosis, and multilevel degenerative disc disease (E003). CT of the abdomen and pelvis revealed an irregular soft tissue mass at the left posterolateral bladder base involving the ureterovesical junction with left ureteral obstruction, highly suggestive of neoplasm, along with numerous lytic bone lesions in the pelvic girdle with associated soft tissue masses consistent with metastatic disease (E004). An interventional radiology biopsy of the right iliac soft tissue mass was performed (E007). Pathology confirmed metastatic carcinoma consistent with urothelial carcinoma, with tumor cells positive for CK7, CK20, P40, Uroplakin, and Gata-3, and focal positivity for CK5 (E008). The clinical presentation demonstrates metastatic urothelial carcinoma with spinal and pelvic bone involvement, primary bladder tumor with ureteral obstruction, and acute kidney injury secondary to urinary obstruction.

Acute insufficiency fractures and metastatic lesion in L3 vertebral body with left hydroureteronephrosis on MRI spine
Primary bladder tumor at left posterolateral bladder base with ureteral obstruction and multiple lytic bone lesions with soft tissue masses in pelvis on CT
Interventional radiology biopsy of right iliac soft tissue mass performed
Pathology confirmation of metastatic carcinoma consistent with urothelial carcinoma with characteristic immunophenotype (CK7+, CK20+, P40+, Uroplakin+, Gata-3+, focal CK5+)
Laboratory evidence of systemic disease burden and acute kidney injury from ureteral obstruction
